title: The organization computer launches in the customer account
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** the assume-role story and the account record story
- **Runs in parallel with:** nothing
- **Unblocks:** paid enablement

---
The behavior the whole epic exists for. Compute for an organization runs under the customer AWS account, using the assumed role, and its cost lands on their bill.

This is what makes the floated price safe, and it is also the strongest thing on the pitch page: the computer runs in their account, on their network, under their logging. Data never leaves. That story sells to buyers who would never accept a hosted agent with a shell.

The failure that matters most is silent fallback. An organization whose cross-account role cannot be assumed must refuse to start a computer, not quietly start one in the Anthus account — which would work, would look fine, and would put a customer workload and its cost somewhere neither party agreed to.

**Done when:** the scenarios exist and fail for the right reason.

comments.text:
Feature: Cross-account provisioning

  Scenario: Compute for an organization runs in the customer account
    Given an organization provisioned into a customer AWS account
    When its computer starts
    Then the instance is launched in the customer account
    And no compute for that organization runs in the Anthus account

  Scenario: An unreachable customer role refuses rather than falls back
    Given an organization whose cross-account role cannot be assumed
    When its computer is asked to start
    Then the start is refused with a provisioning error
    And no instance is launched in the Anthus account
